title: Why Should We Pray For Others
paragraphs: The Power and Purpose of Praying for Others

Prayer is a central part of the Christian life, not only as a means of communicating with God, but also as a way of expressing love and concern for others. But why does Scripture call us to pray for others? What happens when we intercede on behalf of friends, family, neighbors, or even strangers? This study explores biblical reasons and motivations for praying for others, grounding our practice in the teachings and examples found in God’s Word.
Biblical Commands to Pray for Others
Scripture repeatedly instructs believers to pray for one another. The call to intercessory prayer isn’t optional—it’s a vital part of Christian obedience and love.
I exhort therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings, be made for all men. - 1 Timothy 2:1 ASV
Paul urges Timothy to lead the church in making prayers for “all men,” emphasizing the breadth of our concern. This includes leaders, neighbors, and even those we may not know personally.
Confess therefore your sins one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The supplication of a righteous man availeth much. - James 5:16 ASV
Praying for one another is linked to mutual healing—spiritually, emotionally, and sometimes physically.
Following the Example of Jesus
Jesus, our ultimate example, frequently prayed for others. In His high priestly prayer, He interceded for His disciples and for all believers:
Neither for these only do I pray, but for them also that believe on me through their word. - John 17:20 ASV
If Christ Himself prayed for others, we are called to follow in His footsteps, seeking God’s will and blessing on their lives.
Participating in God’s Work

When we pray for others, we join God in His redemptive work. Prayer is one of the means God uses to accomplish His purposes on earth. Paul was constantly asking believers to pray for his ministry, recognizing its spiritual impact:
Brethren, pray for us. - 1 Thessalonians 5:25 ASV
Through prayer, we stand in the gap for others, uphold them in their struggles, and invite God’s power and provision into their circumstances.
Expressing Love and Unity
Praying for others is a practical expression of Christian love and unity. It reflects the heart of Christ and fosters deeper relationships within the body of Christ:
Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ. - Galatians 6:2 ASV
Prayer is one way we “bear” the burdens of others, bringing their needs before God and showing that they are not alone.
Spiritual Warfare and Protection
The Bible teaches that prayer is essential in spiritual warfare. We are urged to pray for all the saints as a means of standing strong against the enemy:
With all prayer and supplication praying at all seasons in the Spirit, and watching thereunto in all perseverance and supplication for all the saints. - Ephesians 6:18 ASV
Our prayers can serve as a shield for others, asking God to protect, strengthen, and deliver them from evil.
Praying for Enemies
Jesus’ teaching goes further—He calls us to pray even for those who oppose or mistreat us:
But I say unto you, love your enemies, and pray for them that persecute you. - Matthew 5:44 ASV
Such prayers reflect the radical grace of God and invite transformation, both in our own hearts and in the lives of those we pray for.
Conclusion: The Joy and Privilege of Intercession

Praying for others aligns our hearts with God’s purposes and makes us partners in His kingdom work. It demonstrates love, builds unity, and releases God’s power into the lives of those around us. Let us be faithful in lifting others before the throne of grace, trusting that God hears and responds according to His perfect will.
